text:
alex: heads-up — turned on v2 routing affinity by default in canary this morning. noticed a spike in client quota hits for a handful of customers. anyone else seeing this?

maya: saw the spike. seems correlated with the header rename we shipped (X-RDW-CLIENT -> X-Client-Id) — some clients still send the old header, so routing ended up assigning them to multiple buckets. quota double-counting. :grimacing:

ben: ohhh that explains the weird billing telemetry i pulled. i saw two distinct client_ids for the same org in the last hour. sample logs: ```"headers": {"X-Client-Id": "org-123", "X-RDW-CLIENT": "org-123"}``` and in other requests only one header present.

alex: thanks. next question — what's our preferred mitigations? options: 1) server-side normalization that prefers X-Client-Id if both present, 2) temporary affinity mapping for the old header for 30 days, 3) roll back default.

dana: prefer (1) + (2) as a safe rollout. normalization is cheap and avoids client churn. mapping with telemetry gives us migration signal.

maya: +1 to normalization. also want a console banner for affected orgs with counts (duplicated buckets). Can the dashboard show "unique clients after normalization" vs "raw header variance"?

ben: i can add a small telemetry probe: emit label `affinity_key=normalized|raw` and `client_coalesce=true|false`. then dashboards can pivot. will add a sample query to the rollout doc.

infra-bot: deploy queued: routing-normalizer v0.1 -> canary (2023-11-18T07:12:34Z).

alex: great. let's also rate-limit the normalization change for 1% of traffic first so we can validate cost/latency. we don't want to affect throughput on high-QPS orgs.

maya: agreed. add a guard: if request.rps_for_org > 200 then bypass normalization until we validate. we can bump after looking at trace percentiles.

ben: done. telemetry: added labels and a sample datadog query. putting the query in #eng-platform-dashboards PR.

alex: for the console UX, product asked that we surface a migration tile per org with counts, example affected header combos, and a suggested action (send X-RDW-CLIENT header or update SDK). dana — can ops own the wording?

dana: will draft wording. keep it short: "Your traffic includes multiple client headers which may cause duplicate quota accounting. We recommend migrating to X-RDW-CLIENT."

maya: also add an opt-out toggle in the org settings: "Enable legacy header coalescing (temporary)" — default off. legal/compliance asked for an audit log of toggles.

alex: good call. infra: add an event to audit-log when someone toggles that. we need retention 90d.

infra-bot: deploy success: routing-normalizer v0.1 -> canary (2023-11-18T07:14:02Z).

ben: early signals look good — 1% sample showed 98% coalescing success and no latency regressions in p50/p95.

maya: i'll send a brief note to @customer-ops for the top 5 affected customers so support can preemptively reach out. also adding a console banner for those orgs.

alex: plan for rollforward: 1) monitor telemetry for 48h, 2) expand normalization to 10% then 100% if stable, 3) enable console migration tile, 4) enable legacy coalescing opt-in for specific orgs for 30 days, 5) schedule post-mortem doc on lessons/communication.

dana: i'll own the post-mortem and the external comms template.

ben: leaving the datadog link in thread: https://app.datadoghq.com/graph/embed/xyz?from=now-2h&to=now — shows duplicate client counts vs normalized counts.

alex: thanks all. quick question — do we want an automatic fallback rule in routing if a client is missing both headers? current behavior is route-by-ip, which sometimes splits orgs across regions. might be risky.

maya: we should add a hashed-session affinity fallback (cookie) for missing header cases — consistent for 24h. but need privacy review. file a ticket for privacy and make default TTL 6h until approved.

sre-oncall: note — i set an alert on aggregated duplicate client rate > 0.5% over 5m. will watch during rollout.

alex: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll reconvene in 24h or earlier if alerts fire. :thumbsup:
